model.architecture: The 4B backbone is Qwen3-4B-Instruct (Qwen3ForCausalLM), so it rides the existing Qwen3 converter and runtime directly.

variants.quantization: int4 block 32 weights (symmetric) + OCTAV optimal-clipping; embeddings INT8 (externalized section); KV cache 4096

platform_notes: Google AI Edge Gallery v1.0.16+ can import litert-lm models directly from Hugging Face inside the app (tap +); manual adb steps only for older builds or sideloading.
A 4B int4 build needs ~2.5 GB free RAM on the phone; reboot first if memory is tight.
iPhone 17 Pro: main weights section ~2.11 GiB (block 32) / ~1.94 GiB (block 128); both load, externalizing the embedder is sufficient for iOS.
Galaxy S26: XNNPACK additionally takes 1 of the 4 nodes in decode_embedder and prefill_embedder_128; the runtime accepts that split.
Reproducibility: GPU rows repeat to within ~1%; CPU rows are noisier (treat the CPU column as accurate to roughly ±7%).
Recommended file: use model.litertlm (block 32) unless decode latency dominates — full parity with bf16, loads on iPhone, Android and desktop alike.
The desktop (M4 Max) rows are this file; the iPhone figure comes from the 2026-06-27 on-device platform matrix, which does not state a run count or prompt.

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (3270 ops across 2 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); same-device control for an existing GPU row on this handset

known_issues: Identity: asked "what is your name?" the model answers "I am Qwen…" — inherited from the base model (the bf16 original behaves identically), not a conversion artifact.
